{ "rules": [
    "Model forecasts lag behind price turning points, especially at market bottoms where they undershoot the true reversal levels.",
    "Sentiment momentum (rising sentiment) provides a reliable signal to adjust forecasts upward when model-based bottoms look too low.",
    "When sentiment turns negative (falling sentiment), forecasts need to be lowered more aggressively than the model suggests to avoid overshooting current levels.",
    "The gap between model forecasts and true outcomes increases at extreme sentiment levels (1.0 or 0.0), requiring more aggressive correction than sentiment would suggest.",
    "Model-based mean reversion works reasonably well for price levels but needs sentiment-based momentum adjustments to avoid lagging behind actual price movements.",
    "When price has been trending strongly, model-based extrapolation creates more error than when price is range-bound and showing mean reversion behavior.",
    "Sentiment divergence from price (e.g., rising prices with flat/bottom sentiment, or falling prices with strong bullish sentiment) signals that the model is missing the real market dynamic."
] }
